name: Serpent's Coil
reason: Technique name coined in the Western fantasy register for a common body-conditioning art; no named counterpart was found in the aligned source chapters (~ch 150-155).
description: A common body-conditioning art from the Eastern Territory, typically one of several styles fighters practice before reaching the Flesh-Honing Stage. In Ep 164 an ordinary armored warrior surprises Zane by wielding Serpent's Coil with unusual skill.

name: Dad
reason: Generic kinship term used in dialogue by various minor characters; not a distinct entity.

name: Lady Novak
reason: Honorific form of Isla Novak ('Isla Novak' appears 55x in episodes, 'Lady Novak' 11x); the character localizes Su Lingyun, Zane's female mentor and the empire's princess.

name: Great Houses'
issues: Terminology drift: Eps 39-178 occasionally say 'Great Houses' for the noble families, while 'Legacy House(s)' is the show's canonical term.
reason: Possessive surface variant of 'Great Houses', a non-canonical synonym for the canonical 'Legacy Houses'.

name: Shadow Vitality
reason: Named with the canonical 'Vitality' energy term (an early draft 'Shadow Aether' was corrected); it most plausibly renders Zane's dark Sky Demon/Heavenly Demon True Qi from the source, whose corrupting-devouring behavior matches the Ep 266 lotus-corruption scene.
description: Zane's shadow-element Vitality manipulation, first used underwater in Eps 180-181. It carries a corrupting influence: in Ep 266 it blackens an exquisite red lotus arrangement, turning each crimson flower diseased black.

name: Fourth-Level Adept
reason: The adaptation renders the source's numbered sub-levels within a cultivation realm as numbered levels of the localized 'Adept' stage.
description: A specific rank within the Adept cultivation stage, used dismissively by antagonists in Eps 404 and 485 to belittle a fighter ('a nobody, a mere Fourth-Level Adept').

name: Brady
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name; 'Brady' replaces the grandmaster blacksmith Wang Dai, who in the source 'had only made two immortal weapons in his life' exactly as Ep 210 says Brady 'had only ever forged two mythic weapons'.
description: A master craftsman famed for having forged only two Mythic Weapons in his life, which alone made his name known across the world, though Chase (source: Che Daozi) is far more renowned. Brady forged Jacob's weapon, telling him a drake's soul remnant was sealed inside its ancient bone.

name: Farrell
reason: The source's unnamed Crown Prince of the Burning Heaven Empire was given the US-style name 'Farrell' to fit the adaptation's Western court setting.
description: The Crown Prince of the empire, described in Ep 344 as his mother's 'own flesh and blood'. His source counterpart is the Crown Prince whose Eastern Palace is sealed and who is placed under de facto house arrest amid palace intrigue (~ch 331).

name: Earthen Armor
reason: Source technique 'Earth Spirit Battle Armor' (Zhou Tong's earth-attribute defensive trump card, ~ch 228) was shortened to 'Earthen Armor' for the Western fantasy register.
description: Langdon's earth-based defensive Vitality technique, boasted to withstand a direct strike from a Soul master. It mimics the properties of the land, dispersing the force of any blow across its entire surface, but Zane's raw striking power overwhelms it in the arena (Eps 237-238).

name: Primordial Vitality
issues: Terminology split: Eps 257-264 call the raw heaven-and-earth energy 'Primordial Vitality' while Eps 295-307 call the same concept 'Primal Vitality'; one term should be standardized.
reason: Same concept as 'Primal Vitality' (the raw ambient energy warriors absorb and convert, source 'World's Yuan Qi'); the earlier episode range simply used a different adjective.

name: Sovereign’s Blade
reason: Artifact name coined by the adaptation; no corresponding named weapon was found in the aligned source chapters (~ch 253-255).
description: A prized artifact wielded by a Soul Realm master during the tournament arc (Eps 266-268), said never to have left its master's hand in battle until it nearly slips from his faltering six-point grip.

name: Shayna
issues: Gender mismatch: episodes consistently portray Shayna as female ('her machete', 'she channeled her Vitality', Ep 280), but the matched source character Xie Yun (the Three Layered Waves saber user who fights Pei Tianyao/Patrick in ch 267) is male (m11/f0).
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name; 'Shayna' replaces Xie Yun, the top saber disciple whose three-chop Three Layered Waves duel against Pei Tianyao (Patrick) is adapted in Ep 280 - with the character's gender flipped to female in the episodes.
description: A top fighter from Skytop Peak and one of the elite inner disciples of the Thirty-Three Peaks (Eps 258-280). Fights Patrick in the ring with a heavy machete, unleashing the three-strike 'Reaper's Chop', each blow carving the air with thunderous force.

name: Zane’s Streamer
reason: Possessive mention of Streamer, Zane's signature Mythic Weapon sword (source: Flowing Light Sword).

name: Celestial Blade Illustration
reason: The literal source term 'Heavenly Sword Diagram' was renamed 'The Celestial Blade Illustration' to fit the Western fantasy register of the adaptation.
description: A legendary sword-cultivation diagram said to contain supreme, supernatural mysteries of the blade; in the source it appeared 875 years ago and set off a reign of terror as sects and clans fought to claim it. In Ep 296, Finn is called a once-in-a-generation genius for having glimpsed its mysteries, allowing him to wield heavenly power.

name: Primal Vitality
issues: Terminology split: the same raw heaven-and-earth energy is called 'Primordial Vitality' in Eps 257-264 and 'Primal Vitality' in Eps 295-307; one term should be standardized.
reason: The source's 'World's Yuan Qi' (the ambient energy of heaven and earth) was localized as 'Primal Vitality', building on the canonical 'Vitality' energy term.
description: The raw, untamed energy between heaven and earth. Warriors normally absorb it during training and convert it into their own Vitality before use, but the Celestial Blade technique draws upon it automatically, beyond the wielder's conscious control (Ep 295).

name: Blood Evil Force
reason: The source's technique name 'Blood Evil Force' was carried over unchanged, already fitting the adaptation's register.
description: A slaughter-path technique taught by the Blood Prisoner. In the source it is an Earth-class technique whose Dao of Slaughter makes it comparable to a Heaven-class one; cultivating it requires heavy killing. Bryson (source: Luo Bingquan) learned it from the Blood Prisoner and amassed shocking amounts of Malice doing so (Eps 332-335).

name: Radiant Hall
reason: Localized name for the palace hall where the princess is confined; the source's corresponding palace residence (~ch 331, Su Lingyun's house arrest) is not named in the available evidence.
description: A softly lit hall in the Imperial Palace where Her Highness (Isla) is kept under house arrest, staffed only by a few essential servants with no one else allowed near (Eps 338-346). Cut off from all news, she can only guess at how Zane fares in the All Peaks Competition.

name: Stone Tablet
reason: Source term 'stone tablet' (the milestone tablets of the sect entrance trial, chs 20-21) was carried over directly.
description: Milestone markers that trial-takers must reach during the sect's entrance examination; in Eps 34-36 Zane pushes toward the next gleaming Stone Tablet in the distance while braced for ambush.

name: Spatial Sanctum
reason: The adaptation's unified term for a personal spatial storage space, rendering the source's interspatial storage treasures for the Western fantasy setting.
description: A personal pocket-space in which a cultivator stores items, used across the show's later arcs (Eps 353-1223): Zane places tokens in his Spatial Sanctum, and a Soulbound Sect rival draws the sword Regis-Bane from his. Possessing one is rare enough to draw surprise (Ep 908).

name: Crimson Crucible
reason: Competition name coined by the adaptation for the Crimson Sect's internal tournament; no named source counterpart appears in the aligned chapters (~ch 344-352).
description: The Crimson Sect's equivalent of the Skyreach Sect's All Peaks Competition (Eps 355-363). Alistair placed first and Adler placed third.

name: Ghost-Faced Spiders
reason: The source creature name 'Ghost-Faced Spider' (chs 355-360) was carried over unchanged.
description: Venomous spider monsters encountered on the trial island (Eps 367-373). Though the ones people usually run into are tiny, these swarm from the trees in dozens, fangs glistening; in the source their poison kills or paralyzes on a single bite, and Zane scatters them with cyclones of sword intent.

name: Apex of Spear Intent
reason: The source term 'Perfect Spear Intent' (comprehended by Zhuo Bufan, ~ch 371) was localized as 'Apex of Spear Intent', matching the show's 'Apex of Sword Intent' naming scheme.
description: Frank's highest level of spear mastery, the spear-user's equivalent of the Apex of Sword Intent (Eps 384-386). It is pure Spear Intent rather than Vitality-based, and the power it contains is described as unbelievable.

name: Garrett
issues: Possible merged/colliding name: in Ep 39 'Garrett' (addressed as 'Mister Garrett') is a Legacy House young master observing The Gauntlet who comments on a separate character named Caleb, yet Eps 1057-1062, roughly 1000 episodes later, feature a 'Caleb Garrett' in the Misty Cloud arc - two apparently different characters sharing the name.
reason: US-style surname assigned to a Legacy House young master; no confident source counterpart identified for either episode range.
description: In Ep 39, a shrewd Legacy House young master at The Gauntlet whose Nature Level bodyguard, a veteran of The Crucible, warns him that the Core Strength 'nobody' Zane is dangerous. A 'Caleb Garrett' later appears in Eps 1057-1062, watching Zane before being sent crashing through walls in a fight.

name: House Fane
reason: US-style noble house name assigned to one of the source's landowning clans; the specific source clan is not confirmed by the available evidence.
description: A noble house (Eps 41-46) counting Chris and Joe Fane among its members. Its influence runs deep in the sect: the mentor of Dragon's Tooth Peak is a member of House Fane first, and crossing the house is said to seal one's fate.

name: Steward Shaw
issues: Localized surname 'Shaw' collides with the established Liam Shaw family name, though the source counterpart (Deacon Xiao of the Cloud Hall) is unrelated.
reason: Source 'Deacon Xiao' of the Cloud Hall was localized as 'Steward Shaw' (Xiao -> Shaw phonetically); the Ep 410 scene with his voice cutting over the warning flute mirrors the source chapter directly.
description: A steward of the Cloud Hall who commands the practice rooms; in Ep 410 his voice booms through the hall over the wailing warning flute, ordering all disciples out, then demands with barely contained rage to know who was responsible.

name: Morphen
issues: Name drift: episodes use both 'Saint Morphen' (81x) and 'Saint Morphens' (34x) for the same Cloud Hall Saint; 'Saint Morphen' is the majority form and should be standardized.
reason: Bare-name mention of Saint Morphen, a Saint-level elder of the Cloud Hall.

name: Dragon Crystal Pendant
reason: Item name coined by the adaptation; no corresponding named token appears in the aligned source chapters (~ch 417-421).
description: A pendant carried by a young master that functions as an access key: in Ep 434 he presses it against a circular glyph on the sixth floor to unlock the way (Eps 430-434).

name: Soul Realm Zane
reason: Extraction artifact joining the cultivation stage 'Soul Realm' with the name 'Zane'; both are already covered by their own entities.

name: Diabolic Duo
reason: Epithet coined by the adaptation for the villain pair Graves and Roman Stryker; no equivalent collective name was found in the aligned source chapters (note: NOT 'Twin Reapers').
description: The villain pair Graves and Roman Stryker (Eps 77-85). Ep 77 marks their defeat: 'The Diabolic Duo had fallen.'

name: Dragon Scale Shards
reason: Localized rendering of the dragon scales tied to the Cobalt Dragon (source Qinglong), whose scales are a central power source in the novel; styled as 'Dragon Scale Shards', two words, NOT 'Dragonscale Shards'.
description: A material linked to Zane's draconic power (Eps 81-84). In Ep 82 incredible power erupts from the Dragon Scale Shards and flows into Zane's own energy as he throws a punch.

name: Glenn
reason: US-origin name assigned to a minor observer figure in the Dragon Castle arena arc; no confident source counterpart identified in the aligned chapters (~ch 66-70).
description: A cautious observer who analyzes the arena situation with measured care, his features concealed beneath the dark fabric of the Shadow Cloak (Eps 81-83).

name: Binding Ring
reason: Localized name for the ring-type weapons of Zane's arena opponent; the source counterpart (Liu Cunshi fights with several named rings in chs 68-71, e.g. Thick Earth Ring, World Annihilation Ring) is not pinned to a single term.
description: Ring-type weapons habitually used by Zane's arena opponent in Ep 83; one of them notably 'looked different from his usual Binding Rings', hinting at a hidden trump card.

name: Ghost Orchids
reason: Material name coined by the adaptation; the term appears nowhere in the source corpus, so it either renames an unidentified source herb or is an invention.
description: A rare botanical material appearing in Eps 90 and 93, during the auction and crafting arc.

name: Adept-tier
reason: Adjectival fragment of the 'Adept' cultivation stage, which is already covered by its own entity; not a distinct entity.

name: Alec
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name; 'Alec' replaces Old Hou, the chief auctioneer of the Tianlu Auction House, who personally presides over the same grandmaster-manual auction adapted in Eps 97-99.
description: The auctioneer presiding over the great auction in Eps 97-99, calling bids from the stage as he presents a manual holding a lifetime of Barrett's forging knowledge. His source counterpart, Old Hou, is the Tianlu Auction House's veteran chief auctioneer who appears in person only for the largest sales.

name: Sector Lord
reason: The source title 'Realm Lord' / 'World Lord' (ruler of an entire great world) was localized as 'Sector Lord' to fit the adaptation's register.
description: The title held by the supreme ruler of an entire realm or world (Eps 636-1232). Yolande is the Sector Lord of the Infinite Realm, the human race's own world lord; in the source, Realm Lords such as the World Lord of the Curses command power spanning hundreds of great worlds.
